Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second chapter to unfold! The two umpires are out there in the middle. Afghanistan players have scattered to take their respective fielding positions. Saif Hassan and Mohammad Naim will be the opening pair for Bangladesh. Azmatullah Omarzai will be starting with the new ball with two slips in place. Away we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

So, 294 is the target set on the board. Afghanistan will be keen to find some early breakthroughs to set the tone of the match. The surface has been tricky to bat on, with its slower nature making it difficult for batters to find timing and clear the ropes. There has been a noticeable turn and bounce on offer for the spinners, but under lights, will it get any easier to bat? We shall find out. The chase is coming up shortly!

Trails of wickets started falling after 173-2 in the 32nd over, and in no matter of time, it was 188-5 in 38 overs. Saif Hassan, from Bangladesh, is the man who took care of the top order single-handedly by picking three wickets. Azmatullah Omarzai and Mohammad Nabi tried to anchor the inning, but Bangladesh had already found their way back to the game. It was Mohammad Nabi who stood tall till the end of the inning and had a sensational knock of 62 runs off just 37 deliveries. Bangladesh were finding wickets from one end, but they had no answers to the masterclass of Nabi.

Rahmanullah Gurbaz is up for a quick chat. He starts off reckoning that the wicket was challenging, so they are pleased with the total they have put up. Their partnership with Ibrahim Zadran was crucial for the team. He continues that he played sensibly, but the finish from Mohammad Nabi was more pleasing to watch. Ends up saying that they need to focus on defending this total. Their bowlers are confident, and that's key to making things work in the second inning.

The innings took off exceptionally good for Afghanistan, with the picture-perfect start of the opening duo. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran were flying high and enjoying the batting pitch. Bangladesh, in the early stages of Powerplay 1, found a couple of edges, but those never got into the palms of any fielders. They both had a partnership of 99 runs of 98 deliveries before Rahmanullah Gurbaz was dismissed by Tanvir Islam. However, Sediqullah Atal does well to fill the shoes and absorb the pressure on Afghanistan's shoulders. They both contributed 77 runs, but things started to tumble after the fall of the second wicket.

What a thrilling end to the first inning! Mohammad Nabi, you deserve a bow. The 40-year-old really proved that age is just a number when it comes to passion and intensity. Credits to Ibrahim Zadran for scoring 95 runs and giving off a strong start, Nabi's inning at the end was the cherry on the cake for Afghanistan to post the total of 293 runs on the board.

PITCH REPORT - Athar Ali Khan and Owais Shah are pitchside with their insights. They says that the pitch looks dry and flat, with no green top to speak about. It's a good surface for batting, but it hasn't yielded high-scoring games so far. The key is to be patient and play the long game. Rahmat Shah's innings was a good example, as he worked hard to accumulate runs, and that's what teams need to do on this surface. For Bangladesh, it's crucial to adopt a similar approach against Afghanistan. The pitch slows down the ball, making it tricky to hit through the line, and precise footwork is essential

Mehidy Hasan Miraz, skipper of Bangladesh, says that will be fine to bowl first. He agrees that the batters haven't performed in the last game and it's part of the game. The batting department will take more responsibility to perform better. Also says that they will try to restrict their opposition in 200-210. Mentions that under the light, it was skidding in the last match, but this time they are ready. Ends up saying that they have four changes, Mohammad Naim, Shamim Hossain, Nahid Rana and Hasan Mahmud join the playing XI.
